resume: Having the State pay all or part of your lawyer's fees and court costs, for example before the family court judge: 2026 limits, form, exact documents and where to submit the file.
aQuoiCaSert: Legal aid (aide juridictionnelle, AJ) covers, fully or partly, lawyer's fees and court costs if your income is modest. It is useful for proceedings before the family court judge (juge aux affaires familiales, JAF): the child's residence, child support, parental authority. You remain free to choose your lawyer.
quiEstConcerne: Parents whose reference tax income (revenu fiscal de référence) and assets are below the limits, who are bringing or defending proceedings.
Minor children heard by the judge in proceedings that concern them: aid is granted to them without any means test.
Victims of domestic violence, who can obtain provisional aid.
aSavoir: 2026 limits for full aid (reference tax income): €12,957 for 1 person, €15,289 for 2, €17,621 for 3, €19,095 for 4, €20,568 for 5, €22,041 for 6, €23,514 for 7.
If your income is slightly above the limit, partial aid of 55% or 25% is possible. For a single person: up to €15,316 of reference tax income for 55%, up to €19,433 for 25%.
Assets also count (excluding your main home). For 1 person: a maximum of €12,957 in movable assets (savings) and €38,866 in real estate. Exceeding an asset limit rules out any aid.
If the application concerns a dispute with a member of your tax household (for example the other parent during a divorce), the asset limit is assessed individually.

First check your insurance policies (home, bank card, legal protection): if legal protection insurance already covers the costs, your AJ application may be rejected. You must provide a certificate stating the insurer does not cover the costs.
Costs incurred before the decision of the legal aid office (bureau d'aide juridictionnelle) are not covered. Apply as early as possible, before the hearing.
The pleading fee (droit de plaidoirie, €13) and any sums you are ordered to pay (damages, fines) are not covered by the AJ.
Appeal against a refusal: 15 days after notification. Once AJ is granted, legal action must be started within the year.
In an emergency, provisional aid can be granted, with your resources checked afterwards.

documents.detail: Filled in online on service-public.gouv.fr, printed, dated and signed. Mandatory if the application concerns another person, for example your minor child.

documents.libelle: Front-and-back copy of your ID document
documents.detail: Valid ID card or passport. Foreign nationals: residence permit or equivalent document.

documents.libelle: Proof of address less than 3 months old (copy)
documents.detail: Bill, rent receipt. If you are housed by someone: also a certificate of accommodation (attestation d'hébergement).

documents.libelle: Copy of the family record book (livret de famille)
documents.detail: Or equivalent document for a foreign national. Lost book: a free second book from the town hall (mairie).
Download it from your account on impots.gouv.fr. Otherwise, proof of income for the last 6 months.

documents.libelle: Proof of a change in family situation or income
documents.detail: For example a recent separation or job loss: certificate, judgment, France Travail notification.

documents.libelle: Proof of savings and real estate other than your main home
documents.detail: Savings account statements, property tax (taxe foncière), if you have any.

documents.libelle: Certificate from your insurer stating it does not cover the costs (legal protection)
documents.detail: Ask your home, car or bank card insurer.
Depending on the case: summons to the hearing, previous judgment, acceptance letter from the lawyer you have chosen.

documents.libelle: Decision of the legal aid office
documents.detail: Keep it and send it to your lawyer.

etapes.detail: Call your insurer: if it covers the costs, you do not need AJ; otherwise ask for a certificate stating it does not cover them.
Compare your reference tax income (on your tax notice) with the limits, or use the official simulator on service-public.gouv.fr.

etapes.titre: Choose a lawyer if you wish
etapes.detail: You can ask a lawyer to take your case under AJ and attach their acceptance letter. If no one accepts, the head of the bar (bâtonnier) can appoint one.
Cerfa n° 16146 form online on service-public.gouv.fr, or an online application on aidejuridictionnelle.justice.fr with FranceConnect if your situation allows.
Signed form, copy of ID, proof of address less than 3 months old, family record book, latest tax notice, insurer's certificate, summons or judgment. Make a full copy of the file for yourself.

etapes.titre: Submit or send the file to the legal aid office
etapes.detail: Before going to court: the office of the tribunal judiciaire (judicial court) where you live. After: the office of the court handling the case.
Send the decision to your lawyer. If refused, you have 15 days to challenge it.

ou.nom: Legal aid office (bureau d'aide juridictionnelle, BAJ) of the tribunal judiciaire
ou.detail: The one where you live before the case goes to the judge, or the one of the court handling the case. Contact details in the Ministry of Justice directory (town or postcode).
Free service with FranceConnect, for disputes before the ordinary courts (juridictions judiciaires, excluding the Cour de cassation).
Free legal reception and information point, listed in the Ministry of Justice directory.
Free legal information (call cost depends on your operator), without access to individual files.

actions.titre: Legal aid application (copy of the file)
Decision of the legal aid office
Start legal action within a year of aid being granted

datesLimites.detail: Costs incurred before the office's decision are not covered: apply as early as possible.
Time limit to appeal against a decision of the legal aid office, from its notification.
Time limit to take legal action after aid is granted.

aConfirmer: Opening hours and how to submit to the legal aid office: specific to each court, check them in the Ministry of Justice directory.
